explicit_semantic_mappings.119: Closing an existing PR is pull_requests.update with body.state=closed; this is not a separate transport or extra registry entry.
explicit_semantic_mappings.125: Publishing an existing draft release is releases.update with body.draft=false.
explicit_semantic_mappings.28: set_machine_type implements the reviewed machine-type change. Live resize constraints, stop prerequisites and guest effects remain acceptance obligations.
explicit_semantic_mappings.34: Compute operation polling covers zone, region and global resources; unrelated Cloud Run/DNS operations are optional candidates for this explicit family.
explicit_semantic_mappings.121: Labels wildcard includes repository label CRUD plus issue/PR label attachment/removal and milestone-label reads through existing issues.* handlers. These are shared canonical constituents, not aliases to repository label deletion.
explicit_semantic_mappings.122: Milestone close/reopen uses milestones.update body.state; assigning/removing a milestone on an issue uses issues.update and remains a cross-family120 lifecycle obligation. list_labels_for_milestone is required read coverage.
explicit_semantic_mappings.124: Annotated tag objects use git.create_tag/get_tag; they do not publish refs/tags. Lightweight/annotated publication, resolution, movement and deletion use shared refs handlers. Existing engineering-branch authority does not authorize tag namespaces. No fictitious tag delete endpoint or redundant alias is added.
explicit_semantic_mappings.114: Archive is repos.update with archived=true (repos.archive is a fixed-body compatibility wrapper); write.preflight is diagnostic. Missing create remains required, not removed by fixed existing-repository scope.
explicit_semantic_mappings.120: Issue CRUD includes close/reopen via update.state, comments, assignment, labels, dependencies, subissues, issue fields, reactions and suggestions. Repository notifications/events and commit comments are supporting cross-family candidates, not issue CRUD aliases.
explicit_semantic_mappings.123: Discussions use fixed GraphQL documents with server-resolved repository/discussion/comment ownership. Reply creation is comments.create(reply_to_comment_id); answer marking, close/reopen and cursor pagination are distinct required behavior.
explicit_semantic_mappings.126: Existing REST package/version list/get/delete/restore is post-publication management, not package publishing. Repository association and immutable package/version IDs remain necessary; a package-manager publishing adapter is a recorded gap.
explicit_semantic_mappings.130: Check runs and suites are separate objects. Create/update, suite preferences, annotations, list/get and re-request are distinct; GitHub App authority for writes cannot be inferred from successful metadata reads or commit-status authority.
explicit_semantic_mappings.131: Statuses are append-only observations per SHA/context, not an update/delete resource. Create, list and combined status are required; a combined success alone cannot attest a particular context or independent build execution.
explicit_semantic_mappings.132: Deployment create and status create/list/get form this explicit family. Deployment list/get supports independent readback. Deleting deployments is supporting cleanup, not implied by create/status scope. GitHub deployment records are not proof that a workload deployed.
explicit_semantic_mappings.133: Explicit list/update includes get for verification. The environment PUT can create or replace configuration; protection-rule and branch-policy administration are separate candidates, not authorized by this mapping. Existing rules/reviewers must be preserved.
explicit_semantic_mappings.134: Repository secret set/remove requires trusted ciphertext custody and repository public-key binding. rotate is a semantic reuse of set with new ciphertext, not a separate endpoint. Metadata reads cannot retrieve values or prove workload use.
explicit_semantic_mappings.135: Repository variables create and update are separate provider operations; set is PATCH, not an upsert. Environment-variable CRUD shares this configuration family. Lists and exact get are required to verify effects; values are non-secret configuration.
explicit_semantic_mappings.136: Environment secrets use exact environment and key identity; metadata get/list/public-key/set/delete are distinct. Rotation reuses set. Plaintext and secret ciphertext cannot be used as public result evidence.
explicit_semantic_mappings.137: Webhook CRUD, exact get, delivery list/get and redelivery cover the explicit scope. Ping/test and separate config reads/writes are supporting endpoints. Redelivery can trigger external effects and needs exact owned delivery and receiver confirmation.
explicit_semantic_mappings.138: Collaborator invitations/permissions and repository teams are related but distinct. Existing collaborator and invitation handlers plus teams listing do not implement team-to-repository permission grant/change/revoke; the missing lifecycle remains a blocker.
explicit_semantic_mappings.139: Ruleset CRUD, effective branch rules, history/version and evaluation suites are distinct. Effective rules can originate above the repository; readback must not imply authority to edit inherited organization rules.
explicit_semantic_mappings.140: Organization audit is filtered to the configured repository and a bounded date window. Existing owner must actually be an organization with provider entitlement; no substitution of a different organization or audit credential is allowed.
explicit_semantic_mappings.141: Security alert listing includes Dependabot, secret-scanning and code-scanning families; alert get/update and advisory tracking are distinct from enabling a security product. Existing broad candidates are retained conservatively; no security setting is activated.
explicit_semantic_mappings.142: Code scanning includes alerts/instances, analyses, SARIF upload/status, databases, variant analyses, autofix and setup settings. Upload accepted is not analysis completion; asynchronous status and functional outcome verification remain required.
explicit_semantic_mappings.1: GET capabilities uses authenticated action=list and caller-filtered registry records. Provider-specific authenticated_discovery and registry.summary are supporting diagnostics, not the universal catalogue. Canonical system.registry.list execution exposure must be reconciled with the route.
explicit_semantic_mappings.2: GET capabilities/{operation} uses action=describe for the selected operation. Provider discovery is not a universal schema/handler/grant description; reconcile canonical system.registry.describe with this builtin route.
explicit_semantic_mappings.3: Generic operations/{operation}:execute dispatches the selected existing operation contract through shared admission, not a separate provider executor. Durable enqueue and legacy deployment execution are distinct acceptance cases; approve_read is authorization support, not execution.
explicit_semantic_mappings.4: Job route classification uses authenticated database resolution to distinguish durable orchestration.jobs.get from legacy deployment.jobs.get. Execution receipt lookup is system.execution.get; deployment.jobs.status is a compatibility diagnostic, not assumed identical without contract tests.
explicit_semantic_mappings.5: Events use orchestration.jobs.events or deployment.jobs.events after principal-scoped job classification. Cursor pagination and ordering must preserve job isolation; polling records alone do not prove streaming delivery.
explicit_semantic_mappings.6: Cancel routes to the actual durable/legacy job kind. Eligible state transitions, worker cancellation acknowledgement and prevention of further effects are separate from request acceptance; cancel is not forced provider rollback.
explicit_semantic_mappings.7: Retry routes to the actual job kind and only idempotent failed work. Unknown provider effects must reconcile first; a fresh job or changed contract/input cannot inherit retry authority.
explicit_semantic_mappings.8: Rollback routes to system.lifecycle.compensate with exact compensation approval and server-selected source snapshot. Lifecycle get/verify are required readbacks; engineering.rollback.* prepares source recovery but is not universal production compensation.
explicit_semantic_mappings.9: Audit list/verify/checkpoint cover chain integrity and observation. Current HTTP resource filter is treated as an operation ID, not arbitrary target-resource lookup. Resource-indexed audit and retention/access behavior remain requirements.
explicit_semantic_mappings.10: Current plans.validate accepts bounded read-only DAGs and reports provider_dry_run_performed=false, null monetary cost and no tenant execution. Schema/dependency validation is not general provider dry-run, pricing or mutation blast-radius planning.
explicit_semantic_mappings.11: plans.execute records a bounded DAG and plans.get observes its jobs; accepted is not completed. Current read-only owner scope does not implement arbitrary multi-service mutation graphs or tenant execution. Runtime owns shared scheduler/worker orchestration.
